chapter_title: Automated Checks, Cost, and Student Privacy
learning_objective: The learner will examine the scores and evidence of three agents for each of six metrics and choose accept, flag, or check anyway, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** multi-agent-triage
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine the scores and evidence of three agents for each of six metrics and choose accept, flag, or check anyway, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Multi-Agent Review, Human in the Loop, Inter-Rater Agreement (defined in Chapter 3) (all defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 3). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each row the learner commits one of three actions. An action is correct when it matches the Correct action column in Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Reading the triage rule is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Agreement among agents proves a score is right. (2) Only disagreement needs a person. (3) The average of three scores is the right score. **Instructional Rationale:** Triaging results from several agents is an Analyze-level action, because the learner must examine each row's spread and evidence together. Rows that agree with no evidence teach the learner that agreement alone proves little. **Content:** The triage rule, shown at all times: the spread is the highest score minus the lowest. If the spread is > 3, Flag. Otherwise, if any agent quoted no evidence, Check anyway. Otherwise, Accept for a spot check. The three actions: Accept for a spot check, Flag, Check anyway. The six rows (all made up, for Watershed Basics): | # | Metric | Agent 1 | Agent 2 | Agent 3 | Evidence quoted | Correct action | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Readability | 8 | 8 | 7 | All three agents | Accept for a spot check | The spread is 1, and all three quoted evidence. | | 2 | Accessibility | 5 | 9 | 6 | All three agents | Flag | The spread is 4, which is > 3. | | 3 | Open license | 9 | 9 | 9 | No agent | Check anyway | The agents agree and none quoted any evidence. | | 4 | Metadata | 4 | 4 | 3 | All three agents | Accept for a spot check | The spread is 1, and all three quoted evidence. | | 5 | Portability | 7 | 3 | 7 | All three agents | Flag | The spread is 4, which is > 3. | | 6 | Alignment | 6 | 6 | 6 | Agent 1 only | Check anyway | The agents agree and two of them quoted no evidence. | **Provenance:** The rows are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The rule follows the chapter section "Multi-Agent Review" and the agreement rule of Chapter 3. **Rules:** Each row has exactly one correct action, two per action. The spread is computed as the highest minus the lowest of the three scores. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one row with the three scores and the evidence note. 2. The learner chooses an action, and the choice is committed. 3. The sim shows the spread, whether the choice was correct, and the Why text. 4. After row 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 rows in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [action]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The action is [action]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can triage several agents." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed row. **Starting State:** The first row and the three actions. The question shown is "What should a person do with this row?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a spread of more than 3 is flagged, agreement with no evidence is checked anyway, and agreement among agents is not truth.
